headline: C.H. Robinson, a large US freight broker, has agreed to buy its rival RXO for $5.8 billion in cash and shares and says it will use AI to cut costs across the combined company.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score of 5: a large, officially announced deal with an AI cost-cutting plan, in a business outside AI itself.
importance_line: What changed is that two large US freight brokers would merge and the buyer plans to put AI agents into RXO's daily work, which matters to shippers and trucking firms that use either broker, then to RXO's shareholders and staff, then to rival logistics companies, and the doubt is that regulators and RXO shareholders must still approve the deal and the $300 million savings are the company's own estimate.
summary: Supply Chain Dive reports, from the companies' news release and investor presentation, that C.H. Robinson Worldwide will buy RXO, a rival freight broker (a firm that arranges truck shipments between shippers and carriers), in a stock-and-cash deal valued at $5.8 billion that the companies say would create a logistics business of more than $25 billion, with closing expected in the first half of 2027 subject to regulatory clearance and RXO shareholder approval. The buyer says it will apply its “Lean AI” operating model, with AI agents handling work across RXO's operations, to reach about $300 million a year in net cost savings within two years of closing, a figure that is the company's own estimate.
